faq.q: What is an anglerfish's fishing rod?
faq.a: It is a long, flexible spine called the illicium, formed from the first spine of the back fin, which moved forward over millions of years. Only females have one.

faq.q: How does the anglerfish lure glow?
faq.a: The tip of the lure, called the esca, is filled with bioluminescent bacteria. The fish gives them a home and food, and the bacteria give off light. It is a partnership that helps both.

faq.q: How can an anglerfish eat something bigger than itself?
faq.a: Its jaws and stomach stretch a long way, so it can swallow prey up to about twice its own size. In the deep sea, meals are rare, so it cannot afford to pass one up.
asks: Why does an anglerfish have a big mouth?

faq.q: Do male anglerfish fuse to females?
faq.a: In some species, yes. The tiny male bites onto a much bigger female and their bodies and blood vessels join. He gets food from her blood and, in return, provides sperm whenever she spawns.
asks: Why are male anglerfish so small?

faq.a: Most deep-sea anglerfish live from about 200 metres down to well over 2,000 metres, in the cold, dark midnight zone. A few anglerfish relatives, like goosefish, live in shallow water.
asks: Has anyone filmed an anglerfish alive?

facts: The glowing lure of a deep-sea anglerfish contains symbiotic bioluminescent bacteria.
In some anglerfish species, dwarf males permanently fuse to females and share their blood supply.

quiz.say: What makes an anglerfish's lure glow?
quiz.why: Bioluminescent bacteria live in the tip of the lure and make light.

wrong.1: Animals do not have batteries; living bacteria make the light.
wrong.2: No sunlight reaches the midnight zone.
